clue.text: Bluish-grey carpet

definitions.meaning: the colour of roofing stone, a dull blue-grey
to carpet someone is to reprimand them, as to criticise harshly

explanation.surface: A description of a grey-blue rug.
explanation.definitionFit: The stone's colour gives one sense; the verb meaning to criticise severely or reprimand gives the other.

clue.text: Prepare to sell, frame and betray

parts.note: to set someone up is to frame them
to shop someone is British slang for to inform on them

explanation.surface: A trader is framed and betrayed.
explanation.walkthrough: To SHOP someone is British slang for to inform on them.
explanation.definitionFit: Opening a business, ready to trade, is the idiomatic sense.

clue.text: A lake in a high, inaccessible place

parts.note: Erie is one of the Great Lakes

explanation.surface: A lake set high in the mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyrie is an eagle's nest built on a cliff top, out of reach.

clue.text: Deplure river transport that's old

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon
a crate is slang for an old, battered car

explanation.surface: Someone complains about ancient river transport.
explanation.walkthrough: The EXE is a river in Devon; CRATE is slang for a decrepit vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: To execrate is to denounce or detest bitterly.

clue.text: Water clock breaking down in dry places

indicators.note: breaking down suggests the letters of the following words collapsing into a new order

explanation.surface: An ancient water clock fails in arid regions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking down' rearranges DRY PLACES; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek timekeeper measured hours by water dripping through a small hole.

clue.text: Doctor gives firm approval

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm
OK signifies approval

explanation.surface: A physician gives a company the nod.
explanation.definitionFit: To doctor the books is to falsify them, as to cook the books.

clue.text: More insurance for one operating in the field

definitions.meaning: a cricket fielder stationed between cover and mid-off

explanation.walkthrough: EXTRA COVER is a fielding position in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Additional insurance is one sense; a cricket fielding position is the other.

clue.text: Upset class, making mistake

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means the word is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: pupils make up a school class

explanation.surface: A disrupted lesson leads to an error.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' turns PUPILS bottom to top; 'making' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip-up is a minor error or blunder.

clue.text: Can the old become involved in a lot of events?

indicators.note: become involved means the letters get mixed up together

explanation.surface: Can an elderly person join in many activities?
explanation.walkthrough: 'become involved' rearranges CAN THE OLD; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The athletics contest has ten separate disciplines, many competitions.

clue.text: The drier of two rivers

parts.note: the Aire is a river in Yorkshire
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Which of two rivers is less wet?
explanation.walkthrough: The AIRE is a Yorkshire river; R is the standard abbreviation for river.
explanation.definitionFit: A clothes horse or rack on which washing is hung to dry.

clue.text: Produced rose

definitions.meaning: manufactured or made, as a factory makes goods
got up from bed, appeared for duty

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means manufactured in one sense and got up or assembled in another.

clue.text: Contract returning police force to its territory

indicators.note: returning tells us to read the police force and its territory backwards, as a single run

parts.note: the RUC was the Royal Ulster Constabulary, Northern Ireland's police force
NI is Northern Ireland, the territory the RUC policed

explanation.surface: An agreement sends the police back home.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Ulster Constabulary policed Northern Ireland (NI); 'returning' turns RUC NI into IN CUR.
explanation.definitionFit: To contract a debt or illness is to bring it upon oneself, a verb sense.

clue.text: American who wrote essay in verse

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe was an American writer
an essay is an attempt, a try

explanation.surface: An American author writes a composition in rhyme.
explanation.definitionFit: Verse is metrical writing, the same thing as rhymed literature.

clue.text: Boast about a post

indicators.note: about means the boast goes around the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: to bluster is to talk loudly and boastfully

explanation.surface: Someone brags concerning a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts A inside BLUSTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A baluster is a short pillar or upright, such as one supporting a handrail.

clue.text: Walk out over hill and fell

indicators.note: in a down clue, over places the first piece above the second

parts.note: to strike is to walk out on industrial action
a down is a grassy hill

explanation.surface: Workers walk out across the hillside.
explanation.walkthrough: A DOWN is a chalk hill, as in the South Downs of England.
explanation.definitionFit: To fell an opponent is to knock them to the ground.

clue.text: Doubt — when one has it, it is unsettling

indicators.note: unsettling means the words before are disturbed and rearranged

explanation.surface: A thought about uncertainty: having it is disturbing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is unsettling' rearranges the letters of ONE HAS IT IT; 'when' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Hesitation is wavering or indecision, an uncertainty of mind.

clue.text: Rifle drill, for example, is tough stuff

parts.note: to rifle or sack a place is to plunder it
drill is a strong twilled cotton fabric

explanation.surface: Gun practice is a hard thing.
explanation.walkthrough: DRILL is a twilled cotton fabric, not a military exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: Coarse fabric of goat hair or hemp, worn in penance, is a rough material.

clue.text: Missile hit pest

definitions.meaning: a bullet or lump of metal fired from a gun
to strike hard with the fist
a slimy garden mollusc that eats plants

explanation.definitionFit: A bullet, a heavy punch and a shell-less garden mollusc share the one short word.

clue.text: Courage of everyone taking part in stand

indicators.note: taking part in means everyone goes inside the stand

parts.note: a gantry is a stand or frame for barrels or cranes
all means everyone

explanation.surface: Everybody shows bravery by joining in a protest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stand' looks like a protest or a stance, but here it is a frame for barrels; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Gallantry is bravery, especially in battle.

clue.text: Flighty vain girl — but chaste

indicators.note: flighty means fickle and unsettled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A frivolous, conceited girl who is nonetheless pure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flighty' rearranges VAIN GIRL; 'but' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Maidenly and pure, as a virgin is.

clue.text: Type of skinflint, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means a word for skinflint is said out loud, giving a different spelling

parts.note: a piker is a mean, stingy person

explanation.surface: A kind of miser, it is rumoured.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic accent PIKER and PICA sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Pica is a size of printing type, twelve points.

clue.text: Temporal message archbishop is to put out? Quite the reverse

indicators.note: Quite the reverse tells us to read the whole statement before it backwards

parts.note: Cosmo Lang was Archbishop of Canterbury 1928-42
to emit is to give out or put out

explanation.surface: A churchman ought to broadcast a time announcement, or perhaps not.
explanation.walkthrough: Archbishop Lang (Cosmo Lang, of Canterbury) gives LANG; LANG IS EMIT read backwards, as 'Quite the reverse' says, is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The pips broadcast on the hour announce the exact time, a message about the hour.

clue.text: More offensive in private

definitions.meaning: a private soldier, one in the ranks

explanation.walkthrough: A RANKER is a soldier in the ranks rather than an officer; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Ranker is the comparative of a word for foul, and also an enlisted soldier.

clue.text: This sauce suited hard-hearted Louis originally

indicators.note: hearted means the abbreviation goes into the heart of the other word

parts.note: if something suited you it became you
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

indicators.note: originally points to the first letter of the name

explanation.surface: A sauce that pleased a harsh French king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hearted' puts H inside BECAME; 'originally' gives the L of Louis. The sauce is named after Louis de Béchamel.
explanation.definitionFit: A white sauce made from a roux and milk, a classic French preparation.

clue.text: Sweep given medal, thus content

indicators.note: content means the second piece is held inside the first

parts.note: BEM is the British Empire Medal
so means thus

explanation.surface: A chimney sweep receives an award and is pleased.
explanation.walkthrough: BEM is the British Empire Medal, a UK honour; 'given' is a link. 'Sweep' suggests a chimney sweep, but it is the brushing tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A besom is a broom made of twigs, used to brush the floor.

clue.text: Stub female dropped before a programme

indicators.note: dropped means the female abbreviation is taken out of the stub

parts.note: a fag end is British slang for a cigarette stub

explanation.surface: A woman lost her ticket stub before a show.
explanation.walkthrough: A FAG END is British slang for a cigarette stub; 'dropped' removes F, leaving AGEND before A.
explanation.definitionFit: An agenda is a schedule or list of items for a meeting.

clue.text: Name, say, given to American drink

parts.note: e.g. means for example, say

explanation.surface: A name is given to a US beverage.
explanation.definitionFit: Negus is a hot drink of wine, water, sugar and spice.

clue.text: Pure water

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means nothing more than; the noun is a lake or pond.

clue.text: Sudden blow disordered thatch

definitions.meaning: an untidy mass of hair on the head

explanation.definitionFit: A jolt of surprise is one sense; a bushy mop of hair is the other.

clue.text: Public housing almost immediately

indicators.note: housing means the first word holds the second inside it

parts.note: overt means open, public
nigh means nearly, almost

explanation.surface: Council housing provided at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Public housing' reads as council homes, but 'Public' is the outer word and 'housing' the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Overnight can mean suddenly, at once, as in an overnight success.

clue.text: Found in a harem, an exotic princess

annotationWithheld.why: Found in a harem, an exotic princess (9): the scan confirms the text; the anagram of A HAREM AN gives eight letters, one E short of MAHARANEE, and no word supplies the E
annotationWithheld.clue: Found in a harem, an exotic princess

clue.text: Gladiolus typically blooming therein

indicators.note: therein says the letters are found inside the words of the clue

explanation.surface: Gladioli are often vigorous in flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'therein' points to the run inside GladioLUS TYpically.
explanation.definitionFit: Blooming as in flourishing, vigorous and healthy.
